title: Key Witness in Comey Case Attests to Justice Dept.’s Aggressive Tactics
summary: A former aide to James Comey at the F.B.I. said the government had engaged in a “harassment campaign” in its efforts to secure witness testimony.

For more than a year, the Justice Department has gone hard after James B. Comey, the former F.B.I. director, using an array of rule-bending tactics in an effort to satisfy President Trump’s drive to see him charged.


In the three cases filed against Mr. Comey so far, prosecutors have[improperly used search warrants to get evidence](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/12/us/politics/judge-comey-richman-files.html) , made[glaring errors in front of a grand jury](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/17/us/politics/comey-justice-department-misconduct.html) and[enlisted a mafia hit man](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/29/us/james-comey-seashells-trump-secret-service.html) in an effort to prove that Mr. Comey had broken the law.


They also considered treating The New York Times as[Mr. Comey’s co-conspirator in a leak prosecution](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/politics/justice-dept-new-york-times-comey-leak.html) in what appeared to be a bid to breathe new life into accusations that might otherwise have been barred by the statute of limitations.


On Friday night, a new court filing added additional details to a portrait of belligerence, showing just how far investigators have been willing to roam in their pursuit of Mr. Comey.


This summer, the filing said, prosecutors hauled two workers at a New York apartment building in front of a grand jury in Florida after they refused to let an F.B.I. agent inside to serve a subpoena on one of its residents — a longtime confidant of Mr. Comey’s from whom the government wanted testimony.


The prosecutors also threatened to charge the confidant, Daniel C. Richman, with obstruction of justice for supposedly evading the subpoena, though he says that his lawyers had already agreed to accept it on his behalf.
